verdict: Baker Hughes grew revenue 14% to $8.0B as the newly bought Chart business joined the books and orders hit $10.8B, though deal costs cut GAAP profit to $411M for shareholders.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $8.0B, vs $7.0B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.61 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $0.70

segments.name: Oilfield Services & Equipment
segments.note: Oilfield services and equipment for drilling and producing wells — up just 1% YoY, with growth in Europe and Latin America offset by a softer Middle East after a business sale.

segments.name: Industrial & Energy Technology
segments.note: Gas turbines, compressors and industrial technology for energy and data-center customers — up 3%, and the order book star of the quarter.

segments.name: Chart
segments.note: Chart Industries, bought on July 16, 2026 — cryogenic and cooling equipment for LNG, hydrogen and space customers. This was its first quarter inside Baker Hughes, so there is no year-ago comparison.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company day to day — up from $597M a year ago as Chart joined.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new energy technology — roughly flat YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Costs of reorganizing parts of the business — there was no such charge a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of acquired intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology and customer relationships bought in deals, mostly Chart — up from just $10M a year ago.

otherDetail: Other costs below operating profit were $334M, net: $177M of net interest expense plus $157M of other expense, which was mainly transaction costs from business deals.
oneTimers: Transaction-related costs of $158M, mainly for the Chart acquisition and business disposals — reported inside other expense.
Amortization of Chart intangible assets of $143M and a $25M inventory step-up charge from the Chart deal, plus $28M of restructuring costs.
Leaving these items out, adjusted net income was $695M ($0.70 per share) and adjusted EBITDA was $1,415M, up 14% YoY — versus GAAP net income attributable to Baker Hughes of $411M.

takeaways.title: Orders surged 31%
takeaways.text: Orders rose 31% YoY to $10.8B. Industrial & Energy Technology took $5.9B — its second-largest order quarter ever, including 1.1 GW of power equipment for a data-center customer — pushing total backlog (RPO) to a record $46.4B.

takeaways.title: Chart's first quarter
takeaways.text: Chart, acquired July 16 for about $14.2B in cash paid during the quarter, added $888M of revenue and $156M of segment EBITDA in its first partial quarter, and $3.6B of backlog.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit fell on deal costs
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Baker Hughes fell 33% YoY to $411M, even as revenue rose 14% — the gap is deal costs, Chart amortization and restructuring. On the company's adjusted basis, profit rose 2% to $695M.
